messages:
kevin: quick heads-up — after yesterday's coalescer rollout i'm seeing a clear p99 jump when cold cohorts get mixed into continuous aggregation. not a kernel regression per se, looks like hit-rate dilution + queueing interaction.

samira: ugh. can you paste the profile? was this on the new kernel-selection path?

kevin: not the kernel selection change. this is the new slice-cohort coalescer settings + continuous batching window tweak. profile snippet below (from /opt/prof/runner):

```
timeline: 00:00:00 - 00:02:00
requests: 12k
median_lat: 21ms
p95_lat: 120ms
p99_lat: 380ms (spike correlates with KV miss rate rising from 12% -> 38%)
coalescer_mix: cold+hot ratio ~ 1:6 -> 1:3 during spike
batch_size_avg: 8 -> 12
kv_hitrate_prefix: 88% -> 62%
```

marta: key observation: when batch size increases we get more prefix collisions (different prompts in same batch) which prevents effective KV reuse. the coalescer is grouping by arrival time, not by prefix affinity.

jen: so two levers: (1) make coalescer affinity-aware (group by prefix fingerprint), or (2) bias continuous batching window to prioritize smaller batches when prefix locality is low. both have tradeoffs for throughput.

kevin: exactly. i sketched a quick sim this morning — adding a lightweight prefix hash gating reduced p99 by ~120ms on the test cluster but reduced throughput by ~7%.

samira: can you share the sim config? want to run on a couple of workloads (chatty vs completion-heavy). also need to know failure modes: does gating cause starvation for cold tails?

kevin: sim config (simplified):
```
coalescer:
  window_ms: 35
  affinity_gate: prefix_hash_mod: 16  # only merge if same bucket
continuous_batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 50
  prefer_locality: true
```
results: p99 -120ms, throughput -7%, kv_hitrate +18% for hot cohorts, cold cohort latency up ~50ms
```

marta: cold cohort tail increase is expected — they lose the batching amplification. can we do a hybrid: affinity gating for the head of window, and probabilistic merging for remainder?

ops-sre: FYI deploy-bot shows the canary rollout (coalescer v2) yesterday at 02:14 triggered a rollback on a single node due to OOM, might be related to increased per-request KV footprint when affinity gating kept more context in-flight. see deploy details: https://deploys/redwood/coalescer-v2/1745

jen: interesting — OOM could be from more concurrent cached KV warming tasks. maybe need backpressure: limit inflight warmups or async warmup with soft priority.

kevin: agree. plan proposed: 1) run affinity-gated coalescer in canary with cap on warmup threads; 2) add telemetry to tag batches with cohort-mix ratio and kv_delta; 3) evaluate latency/throughput curve across three workloads. will open PR with canary config. @samira @marta want to pair on validation tests.

samira: i'm on it, will run workloads tomorrow morning. also will instrument kernel selection paths to confirm we didn't accidentally route to a slower kernel for mixed batches.

marta: heads-up: if we go affinity-first we should also tweak eviction policy — avoid evicting prefix entries that are likely to reappear in next 200ms. short TTL extension for recently warmed keys gave noticeable improvement in sim.

kevin: good point. adding TTL bump + warmup cap to canary plan. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued: coalescer-v2-affinity-canary on 3 nodes. PR: github.com/redwood/coalescer/pull/412

ops-sre: monitoring dashboards added to the canary (kv_hitrate, cohort_mix, p99_lat_by_cohort). will alert if memory or p99 regress beyond thresholds.

kevin: perfect. will post follow-up with PR link and sim artifacts when ready.
